text:
Platform and workspace overview

This platform appears primarily intended to help teams define, design, govern, and reason about applications throughout their lifecycle while preserving relevant context and decisions.

Capability | What it supports | Example
Conversational analysis | Explains concepts and answers application-delivery questions. | Classify an application as simple, medium, complex, or enterprise-scale.
Lifecycle guidance | Describes work from idea and discovery through production and improvement. | Walk through the complete end-to-end application delivery process.
Architecture guidance | Develops capability-level technical architectures and design principles. | Describe an AI-native local development architecture.
Governance and decision support | Identifies decisions, approvals, risks, and accountable roles. | Outline release-readiness approvals and go or no-go decisions.
Process visualization | Represents workflows and responsibilities as diagrams. | Create a cross-functional application-delivery swimlane diagram.
Application knowledge continuity | Organizes durable facts about purpose, ownership, requirements, design, releases, and operations. | Reconstruct what changed in an application when asked about it six months later.

Inventory limitation: The supplied workspace data does not identify the platform product or provide an authoritative tool and capability inventory. Only the capabilities demonstrated by the conversation can be confirmed; no build or deployment was performed.
